title: My Aussie kids’ first time having lunch at a seaside restaurant in the Philippines…
description:
My Aussie kids’ first time having lunch at a seaside restaurant in the Philippines… and they could not believe the ocean was literally under our table. 🇵🇭🌊

Last time we went home to Daddy Barry’s hometown in Bacolod, our relatives surprised him with a birthday lunch.

We thought it would just be a simple family meal.

But when we arrived… the kids stopped in their tracks.

The restaurant was built right above the water.

You could see the sea moving beside us while we were eating.

For our Aussie kids, this was completely new.

They kept looking down at the waves and asking…

“Mommy… are we really eating on top of the ocean?” 😄

The table was filled with seafood, grilled dishes, and all the classic Filipino flavors.

But honestly?

The best part was not the food.

It was the people around the table.

Grand laughs.
Stories being shared.
Kids running around with cousins.

Moments like this remind me why family travel is so powerful.

Traveling with kids is not just about seeing places.

It’s about reconnecting them to where their story began.

Seeing their dad’s hometown.

Meeting the people who shaped him.

And experiencing a culture that will always be part of who they are.

Interesting travel fact: Coastal dining is a big part of island life in the Philippines. Many seaside restaurants are built on stilts above shallow water so guests can enjoy fresh seafood with ocean views just steps away.

For our kids, it felt like an adventure.

For us, it felt like home.

Huge thank you to our family in Bacolod for that unforgettable day.

Tita Angie and family (our cousins Tonet and Bhab).
Tito Bob and family.
And Tita Dottie and cousin Djon visiting all the way from the USA.

You made that birthday memory extra special for Daddy Barry and the kids. ❤️

Moments like this are exactly why we love sharing family travel stories here on BarBelle EverAfter.

If you believe travel brings families closer together…
